edition.name: Migne PL 4 (1844) via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Ac multis proprius interitus satis non fuit. Hortamentis mutuis in exitium populus impulsus est, mors invicem lethali poculo propinata est; ac, ne quid deesset ad criminis cumulum, infantes quoque, parentum manibus vel impositi vel attracti, amiserunt parvuli quod in primo statim nativitatis exordio fuerant consecuti. Nonne illi cum judicii dies venerit dicent: Nos nihil mali fecimus, nec, derelicto cibo et poculo Domini, ad profana contagia sponte properavimus. Perdidit nos aliena perfidia, parentes sensimus parricidas. Illi nobis Ecclesiam matrem, illi patrem Deum negaverunt; ut, dum, parvi et improvidi et tanti facinoris ignari, per alios ad consortium criminum jungimur, aliena fraude caperemur.
pass_a_gloss: And for many their own destruction was not enough. The people were driven to ruin by mutual urgings, death was offered in turn with a lethal cup; and, so that nothing would be lacking for the accumulation of the crime, infants also, either placed or drawn by their parents' hands, lost what they had attained at the very beginning of their birth. Will they not say, when the day of judgment comes: We did nothing evil, nor, having abandoned the food and cup of the Lord, did we spontaneously rush to profane contaminations. Foreign treachery destroyed us, we perceived our parents as parricides. They denied us the Church as mother, they denied us God as father; so that, while, small and imprudent and unaware of such a great crime, we are joined to a partnership of crimes through others, we are captured by foreign fraud.

choices.why: to emphasize the personal nature of the destruction
to convey the idea of external deceit

choices.english: we perceived our parents as parricides
choices.why: to express the severity of the parents' actions

pass_b_english: For many, their own destruction was not enough. Driven to ruin by mutual urgings, the people offered death to one another in a lethal cup; and, so that nothing would be lacking to complete the accumulation of the crime, infants also lost what they had gained at the very beginning of their birth, either placed or drawn by their parents' hands. Will they not say when the day of judgment comes: We did nothing evil, nor did we spontaneously rush to profane contaminations after abandoning the food and cup of the Lord. Foreign treachery destroyed us; we recognized our parents as parricides. They denied us the Church as mother, they denied us God as father; so that, while we were small, imprudent, and unaware of so great a crime, we were joined to a partnership of crimes through others and captured by foreign fraud.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass B correctly handles the clause 'mors invicem lethali poculo propinata est' (death was offered in turn with a lethal cup) by rendering it as 'the people offered death to one another in a lethal cup', which preserves the reciprocal sense of 'invicem'. All clauses, including the complex final sentence regarding the infants' lack of agency, are preserved in both Pass A and B.
